method: The sample links public publisher records to dated Fed and ECB decisions and speeches. The annual table reports observed coverage, including years without a match. Archive availability and editorial selection affect the counts.

Eligible sources are Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, Financial Times and Reuters. Evidence includes the publisher’s article page, original edition or dated archive entry. Records with a matching research inventory item carry its headline ID.

The action tag describes the meeting step stated or anticipated in the headline. The path tag requires explicit language about future policy. A level is a future direction, a revision compares it with an earlier expected path, and an open path records conditional language or a possible pause. An absent path is unscored.

A market tag records an asset or market direction described by the headline. The separate event-study numbers measure market prices around the central-bank communication. Additional news, publication lags and overlapping releases affect comparisons.

The publication date or publisher archive date identifies the edition. An edition clock can reflect an update. The recorded headline may have changed after initial publication. A preview is classified by its content. It cannot establish the market-implied rate or its probability.

The public export contains editorial paraphrases, coding, original links, evidence types and a fingerprint of each reviewed title. A blank policy path means the headline supplies insufficient directional evidence.
